231: /****************************************************************************
232:  * Name: rk806_read_reg
233:  *
234:  * Description:
235:  *   Read a single 8-bit register from the RK806 over I2C.
236:  *
237:  ****************************************************************************/
238: 
239: static int rk806_read_reg(FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv, uint8_t reg,
240:                           FAR uint8_t *value)
241: {
242:   struct i2c_msg_s msg[2];
243:   uint8_t regbuf[1];
244:   int ret;
245: 
246:   regbuf[0] = reg;
247: 
248:   /* First message: write the 8-bit register address (no stop). */
249: 
250:   msg[0].frequency = priv->frequency;
251:   msg[0].addr = priv->addr;
252:   msg[0].flags = 0;
253:   msg[0].buffer = regbuf;
254:   msg[0].length = 1;
255: 
256:   /* Second message: read back one byte. */
257: 
258:   msg[1].frequency = priv->frequency;
259:   msg[1].addr = priv->addr;
260:   msg[1].flags = I2C_M_READ;
261:   msg[1].buffer = value;
262:   msg[1].length = 1;
263: 
264:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, msg, 2);
265:   if (ret < 0)
266:     {
267:       _err("ERROR: rk806_read_reg(0x%02x) failed: %d\n", reg, ret);
268:       return ret;
269:     }
270: 
271:   return OK;
272: }
273: 
274: /****************************************************************************
275:  * Name: rk806_write_reg
276:  *
277:  * Description:
278:  *   Write a single 8-bit register to the RK806 over I2C.
279:  *
280:  ****************************************************************************/
281: static int rk806_write_reg(FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv, uint8_t reg,
282:                            uint8_t value)
283: {
284:   struct i2c_msg_s msg;
285:   uint8_t buffer[2];
286:   int ret;
287: 
288:   buffer[0] = reg;
289:   buffer[1] = value;
290: 
291:   msg.frequency = priv->frequency;
292:   msg.addr = priv->addr;
293:   msg.flags = 0;
294:   msg.buffer = buffer;
295:   msg.length = 2;
296: 
297:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, &msg, 1);
298:   if (ret < 0)
299:     {
300:       _err("ERROR: rk806_write_reg(0x%02x) failed: %d\n", reg, ret);
301:       return ret;
302:     }
303: 
304:   return OK;
305: }

309:  *
310:  * Description:
311:  *   Return the microvolt value for a given vsel selector of the output
312:  *   identified by rdev->desc->id.
313:  *

316: static int rk806_list_voltage(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev,

318: {
319:   unsigned int id = rdev->desc->id;
320: 
321:   if (id >= RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS || selector >= rk806_get_voltage_count(id))
322:     {
323:       return -EINVAL;
324:     }

326:   if (id >= RK806_ID_NLDO1)
327:     {

337:  * Name: rk806_set_voltage_sel
338:  *
339:  * Description:
340:  *   Program the ON_VSEL register of the given output with `selector`.
341:  *
342:  ****************************************************************************/
343: 
344: static int rk806_set_voltage_sel(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev,
345:                                  unsigned int selector)
346: {
347:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
348:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;

361:  * Description:
362:  *   Read the current vsel selector from the ON_VSEL register.
363:  *
364:  ****************************************************************************/
365: 
366: static int rk806_get_voltage_sel(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
367: {
368:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
369:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
370:   uint8_t val;
371:   int ret;
372: 
373:   ret = rk806_read_reg(priv, reg->vsel_reg, &val);
374:   if (ret < 0)
375:     {
376:       return ret;
377:     }
378: 
379:   return val & reg->vsel_mask;

382: /****************************************************************************
383:  * Name: rk806_enable
384:  *
385:  * Description:
386:  *   Enable (power up) the given output.
387:  *
388:  *   The POWER_EN register uses a write-mask protocol: the low 4 bits are
389:  *   the output state and the high 4 bits are the corresponding update mask
390:  *   (bit0<->bit4, bit1<->bit5, bit2<->bit6, bit3<->bit7).  Only bits whose
391:  *   mask is set are updated by the write, so this is NOT a read-modify-write
392:  *   operation.
393:  *
394:  *   reg->enable_mask holds the low-4-bit state bit of the output.  To drive
395:  *   it on we must write both the state bit (1) and its matching mask bit
396:  *   (state bit << 4).
397:  *
398:  ****************************************************************************/
399: 
400: static int rk806_enable(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
401: {
402:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
403:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
404:   uint8_t value;
405: 
406:   /* state bit set (enable) + corresponding mask bit = (state << 4) */
407: 
408:   value = (uint8_t)(reg->enable_mask | (reg->enable_mask << 4));
409:   return rk806_write_reg(priv, reg->enable_reg, value);
410: }
411: 
412: /****************************************************************************
413:  * Name: rk806_is_enabled
414:  *
415:  * Description:
416:  *   Return 1 if the output is enabled, 0 if disabled.
417:  *
418:  *   Only the low 4 bits of POWER_EN hold output state (the high 4 bits are
419:  *   the write mask), so we test the state bit against the low nibble.
420:  *
421:  ****************************************************************************/
422: 
423: static int rk806_is_enabled(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
424: {
425:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
426:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
427:   uint8_t val;
428:   int ret;
429: 
430:   ret = rk806_read_reg(priv, reg->enable_reg, &val);
431:   if (ret < 0)
432:     {
433:       return ret;
434:     }
435: 
436:   return (val & reg->enable_mask) ? 1 : 0;
437: }

439: /****************************************************************************
440:  * Name: rk806_disable
441:  *
442:  * Description:
443:  *   Disable (power down) the given output.
444:  *
445:  *   See rk806_enable() for the POWER_EN write-mask protocol.  To drive the
446:  *   output off we write its state bit as 0 but still set the matching mask
447:  *   bit so the write actually takes effect.
448:  *
449:  ****************************************************************************/
450: 
451: static int rk806_disable(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev)
452: {
453:   FAR struct rk806_dev_s *priv = rdev->priv;
454:   FAR const struct regulator_desc_s *reg = rdev->desc;
455:   uint8_t value;
456: 
457:   /* state bit cleared (disable) + corresponding mask bit = (state << 4) */
458: 
459:   value = (uint8_t)(reg->enable_mask << 4);
460:   return rk806_write_reg(priv, reg->enable_reg, value);
461: }

467:  *   Voltage table for a read-only rail with a board nominal: only selector 0

472: static int rk806_nominal_list_voltage(FAR struct regulator_dev_s *rdev,

475:   if (selector != 0)

- 实例是静态的：返回的是 `&g_rk3576_i2c[bus].dev`（[rk3576_i2c.c:104](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/rk3576_i2c.c#L104-L105>) 的静态数组里的成员），不进堆，永远不会被 free，所以指针也不可能悬空。

PMIC 初始化失败留下的东西是：I2C1 控制器的时钟还开着、SCL/SDA 两个 pad 还在 AF11。这两件事都没有“恢复原状”的目标状态——I2C1 在这块板上就是给 PMIC 专用的，而 GPIO 那两个 claim 是刻意不还的（[kickpi_k7_regulator.c:322-325](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_regulator.c#L322-L325>) 的注释就写着“一旦 mux，pad 就归控制器所有”）。
